title: HyperTEE: A Decoupled TEE Architecture with Secure Enclave Management
problem: Existing TEE architectures have management vulnerabilities that allow attackers to disclose secrets via controlled-channel and micro-architecture side-channel attacks exploiting the management subsystem.
motivation: TEE security is critical for protecting confidential programs and data in commercial processors against sophisticated side-channel attacks.
method: HyperTEE puts enclave management (the system that oversees and protects secure computing areas) onto hardware that's physically isolated from the main computer, so they can't communicate directly. This separation blocks attackers from using indirect spying techniques—measuring timing patterns or power consumption—to learn secrets about the management system. The design also improves how securely these protected areas communicate with each other, while still being compatible with existing systems.
key_novelty: Isolating enclave management on separate hardware prevents attackers from spying on it through timing and power-consumption patterns.
contributions: Decoupled TEE architecture with physically isolated Enclave Management Subsystem
Defense mechanism against TEE management vulnerabilities and micro-architecture side-channel attacks
FPGA prototype demonstrating <1% area overhead with 1.9-2.0% performance overhead
limitations: The abstract does not discuss specific baseline comparisons or threat model scope limitations.
